skill.name: frontend-design
skill.description: Guidance for distinctive visual design when building new UI or improving existing interfaces. It helps plan palette, typography, layout, motion, and interface copy.
skill.summary: Create subject-specific frontend designs with stronger visual direction, copy, and critique.
skill.author: anthropics

security_audit.summary: Reviewed the only static finding in SKILL.md and found it to be normal design guidance, not system reconnaissance. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or unsafe operational instructions were found in the available file.

static_findings.snippet: Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand, and therefore easier to us

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 47 discusses interface copy and user understanding. It does not request system enumeration, host inspection, credential access, or reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Generic AI interfaces often look interchangeable. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward deliberate visual systems, stronger copy, and subject-specific UI.
actual_capabilities: Guides color, typography, layout, and signature element planning before implementation.
Encourages subject-specific choices instead of common AI design defaults.
Prompts critique of design plans before code is written.
Adds guidance for responsive behavior, keyboard focus, and reduced motion.
Improves interface copy with active voice, clear labels, and useful error states.
limitations: It provides guidance only; it does not include executable code or assets.
It cannot verify the final interface unless the host agent can inspect screenshots.
It relies on the user's brief or the agent's assumptions when details are missing.
It does not replace accessibility testing with real users and tools.

use_cases.title: Shape a New Product UI
use_cases.description: Create a visual direction with palette, type, layout, and one memorable design signature before coding.

use_cases.title: Refresh an Existing Interface
use_cases.description: Replace generic styling with subject-specific structure, clearer copy, and restrained motion.

use_cases.title: Review AI-Generated Screens
use_cases.description: Audit a generated page for default visual patterns, weak copy, and missing responsive details.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Visual Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-design to plan a landing page for [product]. Define the audience, palette, typography, layout, and one signature element.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new page

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-design to review this screen: [describe or attach]. Identify generic choices, then propose a more specific visual direction.

prompt_templates.title: Plan and Build a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-design to create a compact design plan, critique it against the brief, then implement the page in this project.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Design Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-design to compare this interface against its subject and audience. Flag template patterns, copy issues, accessibility gaps, and responsive risks.

output_examples.input: Design a page for a neighborhood pottery studio.
output: A clay and kiln palette supports the studio subject.
The signature element is a rotating vessel preview used with restraint.
Labels use plain verbs for booking, classes, and studio visits.

output_examples.input: Review a dashboard that feels generic.
output_examples.output: The review identifies overused card grids, vague button labels, and weak hierarchy. It proposes a calmer operational layout with clearer status language.

output_examples.input: Improve empty state copy for a project workspace.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests direct copy that explains what is missing, names the next action, and avoids decorative tone.

best_practices: State the product, audience, and page goal before choosing style.
Commit to one memorable design signature and keep supporting elements restrained.
Use screenshots or visual inspection when available to critique the result.
anti_patterns: Starting with trendy palettes before understanding the subject.
Adding motion, numbers, or decorative labels without a content reason.
Using clever interface copy when plain action language would help users more.

faq.question: Does this skill build frontend code?
faq.answer: It guides the design process. The host agent still writes the code using the project stack.

faq.question: Can it redesign an existing app?
faq.answer: Yes. It can critique existing UI and propose more specific visual choices.

faq.question: Does it require a detailed design brief?
faq.answer: No. If details are missing, it asks the agent to define a concrete subject, audience, and goal.

faq.question: Will it use the same style every time?
faq.answer: No. It explicitly checks for common AI design defaults and asks for subject-specific choices.

faq.question: Does it cover accessibility?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for mobile responsiveness, keyboard focus, and reduced motion, but formal testing is still required.

faq.question: Which tools support it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
